title: How the Unabomber's Own Words Gave Him Away

narration: For seventeen years, the FBI hunted a bomber it couldn't name.
What finally caught him? His own words. And his own brother.
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); agent_a: arms_crossed -> stern -> determined -> point_up -> stand; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label '17 YEARS · NO NAME'.

sources.claim_text: The UNABOM bombings spanned about 17 years (1978-1995) without the FBI identifying a suspect.
Kaczynski was identified after the manifesto's publication, when his brother David (prompted by his wife Linda Patrik) recognised the writing and the family's lawyer contacted the FBI.

narration: Between 1978 and 1995, sixteen bombs killed three people and injured more than twenty.

sources.claim_text: 16 bombs, 1978-1995; 3 killed; 23 injured per AP and FBI as quoted by AP (one FBI page says 24), hence 'more than twenty'.
UNABOM was the FBI case name, from early university and airline bombing targets.

narration: In 1995, he made an offer.
Publish his 35,000-word manifesto, and he would "desist from terrorism."
shots.visual_description: cabin interior (night grade); ted (silhouette): sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type -> sit_type_b -> sit_type; camera push/pull; overlays: label '1995', card 'THE OFFER: / PUBLISH HIS 35,000-WORD / MANIFESTO, AND HE WOULD / 'DESIST FROM TERRORISM''.

overlays.text: THE OFFER: / PUBLISH HIS 35,000-WORD / MANIFESTO, AND HE WOULD / 'DESIST FROM TERRORISM'

sources.claim_text: In 1995 the bomber offered to 'desist from terrorism' if the New York Times or the Washington Post published his roughly 35,000-word manuscript.

narration: The FBI and the Attorney General backed printing it,
hoping someone would recognise the writer.
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); agent_a: present; agent_b: read -> stand; camera push/pull; overlays: label 'FBI + ATTORNEY GENERAL', label 'THE GAMBLE'.

sources.claim_text: Attorney General Janet Reno and FBI Director Louis Freeh recommended publication; the FBI's aim was that someone would recognise the author.

narration: On September 19th, 1995, The Washington Post printed all of it.
shots.visual_description: press hall (cold grade); press_operator: stand -> read_newspaper; camera push/pull; overlays: label '19 SEPTEMBER 1995'.

sources.claim_text: The Washington Post published the full text on 19 September 1995 as an 8-page insert, with the New York Times sharing the cost.

narration: One reader, Linda Patrik, suspected her husband's brother.
She urged her husband, David, to read it.
shots.visual_description: kitchen night (warm grade); linda: sit_read -> worried -> present; david: stand -> focused (walks); camera push/pull; overlays: label 'LINDA PATRIK', label 'DAVID KACZYNSKI'.

sources.claim_text: Linda Patrik, David Kaczynski's wife, first suspected Ted and urged David to read the manifesto.

narration: David compared it with old letters from his brother, Ted.
shots.visual_description: kitchen night (warm grade); david: sit_read -> worried; camera push/pull; overlays: svg.

sources.claim_text: David compared the manifesto with Ted's old letters and essays; the family had an outside team (via PI Susan Swanson, ex-FBI analyst Clint Van Zandt) compare them, which judged the same person had probably written both.

narration: An outside analyst judged the same person had probably written both.
shots.visual_description: office day (none grade); examiner: examine -> realise -> stand; camera push/pull; overlays: label 'OUTSIDE ANALYSIS', card 'SAME WRITER? / PROBABLY.'.

sources.claim_text: David compared the manifesto with Ted's old letters and essays; the family had an outside team (via PI Susan Swanson, ex-FBI analyst Clint Van Zandt) compare them, which judged the same person had probably written both.

narration: Early in 1996, through a lawyer, the family went to the FBI.
Analysts found the same unusual twist on an old saying in both:
"You can't eat your cake and have it too."
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); analyst: sit_read -> examine -> realise; agent_b: read -> stand; keyed camera moves; overlays: label 'EARLY 1996', label 'IN BOTH TEXTS', card 'IN BOTH TEXTS: / 'YOU CAN'T EAT YOUR CAKE / AND HAVE IT TOO.' / USUAL: 'HAVE YOUR CAKE AND EAT IT'', svg.

overlays.text: IN BOTH TEXTS: / 'YOU CAN'T EAT YOUR CAKE / AND HAVE IT TOO.' / USUAL: 'HAVE YOUR CAKE AND EAT IT'

sources.claim_text: In early 1996 the family's lawyer, Tony Bisceglie, contacted the FBI and supplied comparison writings.

The manifesto (para. 185) uses the inverted idiom 'you can't eat your cake and have it too'; FBI analyst James Fitzgerald flagged that it matched Ted's known writing. (Which letter it matched is disputed, so the script does not name one.)

narration: April 3rd, 1996. Agents arrested Ted Kaczynski at his tiny cabin in Montana.
Inside, they found a live bomb, wrapped and ready to mail.
shots.visual_description: cabin woods (cold grade); ted: stand -> hands_behind; agent_a: stand -> present (walks); agent_b: stand (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: label '3 APRIL 1996', label 'TED KACZYNSKI', svg.

sources.claim_text: Ted Kaczynski was arrested on 3 April 1996 at his cabin (about 10 x 12 ft) near Lincoln, Montana.
Agents found a live bomb in the cabin, wrapped and ready to mail, plus bomb components and tens of thousands of pages of writing.

narration: In 1998, he pleaded guilty, and was sentenced to life without release.
shots.visual_description: courtroom (cold grade); judge: sit -> gavel -> sit; ted: hands_together -> stern; camera push/pull; overlays: label '1998', card 'JANUARY 1998: PLEADS GUILTY / MAY 1998: SENTENCED / LIFE WITHOUT RELEASE'.

overlays.text: JANUARY 1998: PLEADS GUILTY / MAY 1998: SENTENCED / LIFE WITHOUT RELEASE

sources.claim_text: He pleaded guilty on 22 January 1998 in exchange for life without possibility of release; on 4 May 1998 he was sentenced to four life terms plus 30 years.

narration: David received a one-million-dollar reward.
He pledged most of it to the families of his brother's victims.
The bomber wanted the world to read his words. His own family did.
shots.visual_description: kitchen night (warm grade); david: hands_together -> relieved; linda: arms_crossed -> relieved; keyed camera moves; overlays: card 'AUGUST 1998 / $1,000,000 REWARD / MOST PLEDGED TO VICTIMS' FAMILIES'.

overlays.text: AUGUST 1998 / $1,000,000 REWARD / MOST PLEDGED TO VICTIMS' FAMILIES

sources.claim_text: David Kaczynski received the $1 million reward in August 1998 and pledged most of it to victims' families (roughly $630k-$680k reached them after taxes and legal costs).
Kaczynski was identified after the manifesto's publication, when his brother David (prompted by his wife Linda Patrik) recognised the writing and the family's lawyer contacted the FBI.
